title_en: Official Reply on Issues Concerning Ensuring the Right of Detained Criminal Suspects and Defendants to Choose Defense Counsel According to Law

articles.content_en:
June 25, 2025
Supreme People's Court Supreme People's Procuratorate
Reply on Issues Concerning the Protection of the Right of Criminal Suspects and Defendants in Custody to Choose Defense Counsel According to Law
Fa Shi [2025] No. 9
Higher People's Courts and People's Procuratorates of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court and the Military Procuratorate of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region; and the People's Procuratorate of Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps:
Recently, some Higher People's Courts and provincial People's Procuratorates have submitted requests for instructions on issues concerning how to determine the choice of defense counsel for criminal suspects and defendants in custody. Upon study, pursuant to the relevant provisions of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and the Legal Aid Law of the People's Republic of China, the Reply is as follows:
After a legal aid institution has assigned a lawyer to provide legal aid and serve as defense counsel for a criminal suspect or defendant in custody, regardless of whether the defense counsel has already met with the criminal suspect or defendant, if the guardian or close relative of the criminal suspect or defendant further entrusts a defense counsel on behalf of the criminal suspect or defendant, the entrusted defense counsel shall have the right to meet with the criminal suspect or defendant. After the meeting, if the criminal suspect or defendant chooses the defense counsel entrusted by their guardian or close relative on their behalf to defend them, the People's Court or the People's Procuratorate shall promptly notify the legal aid institution to terminate the legal aid according to law.
